newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks higher, but fading in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks higher, but fading in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were higher but fading from early highs in late Tuesday trade as a big surge in electronics failed to carry other sectors, brokers said.
With 40 minutes left, at 0320 GMT, the index was up 56.71 points or 0.66 percent at 8,697.16, off a high of 8,763.88.
Turnover was a heavy T$149 billion.
Electronics had surged 3.01 percent, with chipmaker Winbond up T$2 to T$45.2.
Financials, plastics and steels were down.
"Electronics alone still can't lead the wider market upward strongly," said Jardine Fleming fund manager George Hou.
"After all, the index had surged for three straight sessions, and investors naturally are worried about possible profit-taking," Hou said.

Constructions fell despite news that Taiwan's finance ministry had auctioned a large piece of state land on Monday in Taipei's commercial district at a winning bid price 40 percent higher than the base price due to intense competition.
"The fact that constructions fell despite the good news also dampened confidence," Hou said.
